title: Deployment Telemetry Workbench for Canary Comparisons
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Build a 'Telemetry Workbench' feature in Console that enables engineers and PMs to run fast, confident canary and A/B comparisons across model variants. The workbench will provide side-by-side cohort comparisons, per-route metric breakdowns, trace links, prompt-output diffs, and an integrated readiness score for auto-rollback. This ticket scopes the product spec, acceptance criteria, and launch checklist for the initial MVP.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console has a new Workbench view that accepts two cohorts (control vs candidate) and a time window. 2) Workbench shows per-route metrics: request count, p50/p95 latency, tokens-per-call, error-rate, cost-per-token, and request-level success/regression counts. 3) Cohort diff panel computes relative change and a statistical significance indicator (paired bootstrap or bootstrap CI). 4) Traces: for sampled requests, links open to tracing UI with cohort tag. 5) Prompt/response diff: top N most-different prompts with example pairs and a simple delta view highlighting token-level differences. 6) Auto-rollback readiness: UI surface that shows whether the candidate meets configured rollback predicates and a link to the rollback runbook. 7) Performance: initial aggregation queries return within SLO (3s) for 30-minute windows on 90th percentile. 8) Feature flag gated and telemetry annotated so we can A/B test adoption.
design_notes:
- Primary compare axis is cohort (traffic slice), not model version; allow mapping of route->variant.
- Use time-aligned windows (shift candidate to align to traffic shape) to avoid traffic skew.
- For statistical testing prefer non-parametric bootstrap to avoid distribution assumptions on latency and token counts.
- Sampling: keep trace and prompt sampling configurable; default 0.5% for traces and 1% for prompt captures to limit cost.
- Diff UX: show both absolute and relative delta with effect size and a red/yellow/green health tile per metric.
- Rollback integration: surface the same predicates used by ENG auto-rollback infra so Console can preview what a rollback trigger would have seen.
tradeoffs:
- Accuracy vs cost: full corpus diffs are expensive; we sample prompts and compute approximate effect sizes. MVP uses bootstrapped CIs over sampled data.
- Latency vs freshness: running real-time diffs for many routes is expensive; MVP will pre-aggregate rolling windows (1m granularity) and compute diffs on request.
- Complexity: to keep UI simple, initial Workbench will show up to 10 routes in side-by-side mode. Larger comparisons will require CSV export for offline analysis.
implementation_plan: 1) Product spec and UX mockups (this ticket). 2) Backend: extend telemetry aggregation pipeline (ENG-4021) to produce cohort-tagged summaries + diffing API (ENG-3987). 3) Trace sampling change deployed (ENG-4102). 4) Console UI: Workbench view, cohort selector, metric tiles, diff table, trace links. 5) QA: synthetic canary runs with seeded regressions. 6) Pilot with two internal teams and iterate. 7) Gradual roll-out with feature flag and telemetry for adoption metrics.
risks:
- Sampling too low may hide regressions.
- Statistical tests misinterpreted by users leading to incorrect rollouts. Need clear UI copy and guardrails.
- Aggregation latency could exceed SLO under high cardinality workloads.
- Security: captured prompt examples must be scrubbed; coordinate with Privacy & Security for masking rules.
